request.spec:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Holds now have a from-date and an optional to-date, and a person can have several of them. All 4 tests in the spec pass under `bin/e2e`.

**Stored data**
- New migration `V31__person_hold.sql` adds a `person_hold` table holding each hold's from-date and optional to-date. It drops the old `person.held` flag.
- Anyone held before the migration gets an open-ended hold starting `0001-01-01`, so their totals don't change.

**Server**
- **Totals rule:** a claim is left out only if it is open (OPEN or PENDING), not bound by a statement, and dated within one of the person's holds. Settled claims and claims bound by a statement always count. The same rule is used for the live totals, period totals and statements.
- **Hold action:** `POST …/people/{id}/hold` now takes `{from, to}` and adds a hold; a blank from-date takes the sheet's today. It writes `PERSON_HELD sheet=… by=… name=… from=…`, followed by any ROLLUP and TOTALS lines the hold caused.
- **Release:** there is no longer a release action, so PERSON_RELEASED is never written.
- **Refusal:** a to-date before the from-date is refused, and nothing is written to the store or the audit file.
- **Person data:** the person's data now includes the list of holds; `held` means "has any hold".

**Front end** (`people.ts`, `people-api.ts`)
- Each person's row lists their holds (`person-hold-line`) and has from/to date inputs (`person-hold-from`, `person-hold-to`). The existing `person-hold-toggle` button adds a hold with those dates.
- `person-hold` shows yes/no for whether the person has any hold.
- The screen's own totals calculation uses the same rule as the server.

Decisions you may want to revisit:
- A hold that only covers past dates still shows "yes", because the request asks for "has any hold".
- Adding a hold with the same dates as an existing one is allowed and creates a second entry.
- "Bound by a statement" means a stated claim that isn't PENDING, which is how the existing code defines it. So a stated PENDING claim inside a hold is left out of the totals.
